text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A27 ran in every trace (200 of 200); in the later window it runs in about 52 in 100 traces, still once per trace where it appears. Its ties thinned accordingly: A14, A15 and A26 each co-occurred with A27 in every earlier trace, usually before it, whereas in the later window they co-occur with it in only about 51–52 in 100 traces [OCC003, REL009, REL013, REL017].
- Three activities absent from the earlier window — A32, A33 and A38 — each run in about 49–50 in 100 later traces, about once per trace where they appear, near the middle of the trace by event order (median relative position about 0.50) [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, POS003, POS004, POS005].
- In the later window, A27 and each of the new activities are near-perfect alternatives: about 50 in 100 traces contain only A27 and about 48–49 in 100 only the new activity, with both together in at most about 1–2 in 100; earlier, every trace had A27 and none had them [REL022, REL023, REL024].
- The new activities run as one block: any two of them co-occur in about 49 in 100 later traces (never earlier), they occur in both orders relative to one another, and their outgoing transitions lead mostly to each other and to A28 [REL028, REL029, REL030, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009].
- The surroundings kept their presence: A14, A15, A26 and A28 still occur in essentially every later trace, as they did earlier [REL010, REL014, REL018, REL025].
- Routing into the segment changed: about 95 in 100 of A26's observed outgoing transitions went to A27 earlier, while in the later window about 51 go to A27, 18 to A33, 17 to A38 and 15 to A32; A14 and A26 precede the new block in about 48–50 in 100 traces, and A15 precedes it in about 30 in 100 (interleaved in about 20) [DIR006, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL014, REL015, REL016].
- Routing out changed too: A28 followed A27 in about 98 in 100 earlier traces, whereas in the later window the new activities precede A28 in about 47–48 in 100 traces, and the distance from A26 to A28 stretches from about 2 steps to about 4 steps in roughly half the later traces [REL021, REL025, REL026, REL027, LAG003].
- A04 became about three times as common (about 19 to 60 in 100 traces) and occurs much earlier in the trace (median relative position from about 0.55 to about 0.17); A14 now routes to A04 in about half of its observed outgoing transitions (about 4 in 100 earlier), usually one step ahead, and A04 leads to A15 in about 87 in 100 of its outgoing transitions [OCC001, POS001, DIR004, LAG001, DIR001].
- A06's participation fell from about 20 to 4 in 100 traces; its successor mix also differs in the later window, but that profile rests on only 8 observations [OCC002, DIR002].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the mandatory middle step A27 was, in the later window, replaced in about half of the cases by a block of three previously unobserved activities — A32, A33 and A38 — which run together in varying order between the unchanged surroundings (A14, A15 and A26 before it, A28 after it) [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL028, REL029, REL030].

The hypothesis is shown directly on several indicator types rather than inferred from a single relation: participation counts for A27 and the new activities [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]; mid-trace positions for the new activities [POS003, POS004, POS005]; the successor split at A26, whose flow earlier went almost exclusively to A27 and now divides between A27 and the new activities [DIR006]; and relational evidence placing the block between A14/A15/A26 and A28, with the A26-to-A28 distance growing from about 2 to about 4 steps in half the later traces, as expected when a block is inserted [REL018, REL019, REL020, REL025, REL026, REL027, LAG003]. Chance is unlikely to explain the pattern as a whole: 55 control-flow items qualified where about 0.7 would be expected without change across 146 tested units, and each item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data [OCC003, REL024, DIR006].

Limitations: zero participation earlier shows only that A32, A33 and A38 were not observed in that window, so a newly added block and a previously rare path that became frequent look identical here [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]. The many agreeing items largely describe the same traces and are not independent confirmations [REL022, REL023, REL024]. The evidence also cannot distinguish one modified flow with an exclusive choice between A27 and the new block from a later window that mixes an old and a new case variant, because the two hardly ever share a trace [REL022, REL023, REL024].

Other differences: A04 now runs in about 60 in 100 traces (about 19 earlier), much earlier in the trace, and typically between A14 and A15 — A14 routes to it in about half of its outgoing transitions and it leads to A15 in about 87 in 100 — a change separate from the A27 substitution [OCC001, POS001, DIR004, LAG001, DIR001]. A06's participation fell from about 20 to 4 in 100 traces, though the accompanying successor shift rests on only 8 later observations and is weak [OCC002, DIR002].
